The activity of succinate dehydrogenase, an enzyme in the Krebs cycle, is used as a measure of the rate of respiration in the mitochondria. The redox reaction catalysed by succinate dehydrogenase is shown in Fig. 8.2.

Fig. 8.2
The activity of succinate dehydrogenase can be measured using a redox indicator.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
(c) Fig. 8.3 shows a ground squirrel, Ictidomys tridecemlineatus.
{{figure:figure_8_3.webp}}
Fig. 8.3
In the winter, the ground squirrel curls into a spherical shape underground and sleeps for long periods. During this time, the ground squirrel switches between two states:
- torpor, when the body temperature is maintained at $10^\circ\text{C}$
- euthermia, when the body temperature is maintained at $37^\circ\text{C}$.
Scientists used the activity of succinate dehydrogenase to investigate the rate of respiration in the mitochondria of ground squirrels. Mitochondria were extracted from liver and muscle samples of ground squirrels. The rate of respiration was measured at different concentrations of succinate and at temperatures that corresponded to torpor ($10^\circ\text{C}$) and euthermia ($37^\circ\text{C}$).
The results are shown in Fig. 8.4.
{{figure:figure_8_4.webp}}
Fig. 8.4
parts.text: Describe the trends shown in Fig. 8.4.

parts.label: (c)(ii)

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
During torpor in ground squirrels, muscle tissue uses more energy than liver tissue.
Suggest one reason for this difference.
